Ommisa CLI

The Ommisa CLI runs on Node.js 18 and above and carries no runtime dependencies. The answer streams to the terminal as it is written; standard output carries only the reply, while the spinner, warnings and quota notes are written to standard error.

Installation

npm install -g @ommisa/cli

Signing in

ommisa login
ommisa login --read-only

The login uses the OAuth Device Authorization Grant (RFC 8628) against the OIML SMART identity service. The command prints a short code and opens the approval page; approving the code completes the sign-in. The credentials are stored at ~/.config/ommisa/credentials.json with mode 0600. The identity service issues a personal access token scoped with the <service>:<read|write|admin> grammar, and it re-judges the token on every request, so revocation ends access within seconds.

Asking questions

ommisa ask "What is the MPE requirement for a load cell per OIML R 60?"
ommisa ask --lang fr "Qu'est-ce que l'EMT d'une cellule de charge ?"
ommisa ask --fresh "..."
ommisa ask --public "..."
ommisa ask "..." --save
ommisa ask "..." --conversation <id>

The command uses the member tier when the machine holds credentials and the public tier otherwise; the tier, the remaining quota and the sign-in instruction are printed with every answer. The --public option forces the anonymous lane even when credentials exist. The --fresh option bypasses the answer caches, the --save option stores the turn as a new conversation, and --conversation continues a stored conversation.

Memory files, conversations and projects

ommisa memories
ommisa memories add "My laboratory" "Class C load cells at 23 degrees Celsius."
ommisa memories rm <id>
ommisa conversations
ommisa conversations show <id>
ommisa conversations new "Load cells"
ommisa conversations rm <id>
ommisa files
ommisa files <project-id>

Memory files that the account holder enables join subsequent questions as context, on the web application and in the CLI alike.

Session and configuration

ommisa status
ommisa whoami
ommisa logout

The environment variables OMMISA_ID, OMMISA_API, OMMISA_CLIENT_ID and OMMISA_SCOPE override the defaults, and the flags --issuer, --api, --client-id and --scope override them per call.

Security posture

The CLI is a registered public client and holds no secret. It requests read and write scopes for the oiml-ai service, and the identity service judges the request against the approving account's standing at approval and at every renewal. The AI service admits the token as a read credential and refuses writes unless the approved scope states a write.

Ommisa is part of the OIML SMART programme — a public pilot. Answers are for information only; the official OIML publications govern.
